newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia military gives poll security assurance.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia military gives poll security assurance.

text.p: Indonesia's military has given an assurance that it will try to maintain security after incidents of mob violence during the nation's election campaign, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Saturday.
Armed forces (ABRI) spokesman Brigadier-General Slamet Supriadi said that as of Thursday, 73 people had died, mostly in traffic accidents, since the campaign began three weeks earlier.
"ABRI has made an all-out effort to maintain security so that people can go about their daily business without fear," Supriadi told reporters on Friday.

Government officials have said that campaigning has been marred by violations of strict rules designed to limit confrontation between supporters of rival parties and lessen the risk of street violence.

Indonesians on May 29 cast their votes in national, regional and district elections for candidates from the ruling Golkar, Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).

The government only recognises these three parties and has rejected the candidates of ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri whose supporters continue to appear in campaigning for the government-backed PDI faction.

The official Antara news agency said Megawati supporters in the East Java town of Malang on Friday injured three members of the security forces in a clash after they tried to take down a Megawati banner at a local teacher training college.
Antara said 15 people were detained in the incident.
The government on Monday banned any banners using the words or images of Megawati as she is not a recognised contestant.

In the West Java town of Bogor, hundreds of Megawati supporters conducted an illegal motorcade while wearing T-shirts with Megawati's image and the words "Solidarity Megawati". Security forces did not intervene.
Witnesses said some of the supporters attacked supporters of her rival Surjadi, removing their party T-shirts and stoning their cars in a few minor incidents.
Megawati had told her supporters before the campaign started not take part in the name of the PDI, but a number of banners bearing her name have appeared at PPP rallies.
The Jakarta Post said dismal turnouts continued to affect the official PDI public meetings and rallies.
The Media Indonesia daily reported that PPP supporters in the South Sulawesi capital of Unjung Pandang stoned the local Golkar office after a rally in the city on Friday.

The paper said PPP and Golkar supporters damaged a number of houses in a spate of stone throwing before riot police dispersed the two sides by firing warning shots into the air. It said nobody was injured.
